transcript.en: Hi. Today we're going to be looking at animals in urban environments
transcript.zh: 今天我们来聊一聊城市环境中的动物，

transcript.en: and I'm going to be telling you about some research on how they're affected by these environments.
transcript.zh: 我会向大家介绍一些关于动物如何受到环境影响的研究。

transcript.en: Now, in evolutionary terms, urban environments represent huge upheavals,
transcript.zh: 从进化论的角度来看，城市环境发生了巨变，这种巨变通常是在数百万年内发生的。

transcript.en: the sorts of massive changes that usually happen over millions of years.
transcript.zh: 这种巨变通常是在数百万年内发生的。

transcript.en: And, we used to think that only a few species could adapt to this new environment.
transcript.zh: 我们过去认为只有少数物种能够适应这种新环境。

transcript.en: One species which is well known as being highly adaptable is the crow,
transcript.zh: 众所周知，乌鸦是一种适应性很强的物种，

transcript.en: and there've been various studies about how they manage to learn new skills.
transcript.zh: 人们已经对乌鸦如何学习新技能进行了各种各样的研究。

transcript.en: Another successful species is the pigeon,
transcript.zh: 另一种具有同样强适应性的物种是鸽子，

transcript.en: because they're able to perch on ledges on the walls of city buildings,
transcript.zh: 它们能够栖息在城市建筑物的墙壁上，

transcript.en: just like they once perched on cliffs by the sea.
transcript.zh: 就像它们曾经栖息在海边的悬崖上一样。

transcript.en: But in fact, we're now finding that these early immigrants were just the start of a more general movement of animals into cities,
transcript.zh: 但事实上，我们现在发现，乌鸦和鸽子只是动物进入城市的早期移民，

transcript.en: and of adaptation by these animals to city life.
transcript.zh: 也是这些动物适应城市生活的开始。

transcript.en: And one thing that researchers are finding especially interesting is the speed with which they're doing this -
transcript.zh: 研究人员发现一件特别有趣的事情，那就是动物适应的速度

transcript.en: we're not talking about gradual evolution here,
transcript.zh: 这并不是缓慢的进化

transcript.en: these animals are changing fast.
transcript.zh: 这些动物的进化速度简直惊人。

transcript.en: Let me tell you about some of the studies that have been carried out in this area.
transcript.zh: 我给大家介绍一下在这方面进行的一些研究。

transcript.en: So, in the University of Minnesota,
transcript.zh: 在明尼苏达大学，

transcript.en: a biologist called Emilie Snell-Rood and her colleagues looked at specimens of urbanised small mammals such as mice and gophers that had been collected in Minnesota,
transcript.zh: 一位名叫Emilie Snell-Rood的生物学家和她的同事对明尼苏达州收集的城市小型哺乳动物（如老鼠和地鼠）标本进行了研究，

transcript.en: and that are now kept in museums there.
transcript.zh: 这些标本现在保存在博物馆里。

transcript.en: And she looked at specimens that had been collected over the last hundred years,
transcript.zh: 她观察了过去一百年来收集的标本，

transcript.en: which is a very short time in evolutionary terms.
transcript.zh: 从进化的角度来看，这是一段很短的时间。

transcript.en: And she found that during that time,
transcript.zh: 她发现，

transcript.en: these small mammals had experienced a jump in brain size when compared to rural mammals.
transcript.zh: 与农村哺乳动物相比，这些小型哺乳动物的大脑尺寸大大增加。

transcript.en: Now, we can't be sure this means they're more intelligent,
transcript.zh: 我们现在无法确定这是否意味着这些哺乳动物变得更聪明，

transcript.en: but since the sizes of other parts of the body didn't change,
transcript.zh: 但是由于身体其他部分的大小没有改变，

transcript.en: it does suggest that something cognitive was going on.
transcript.zh: 这确实表明了发生了一些认知方面的变化。

transcript.en: And Snell-Rood thinks that this change might reflect the cognitive demands of adjusting to city life
transcript.zh: Snell-Rood认为，这种变化可能反映了适应城市生活的认知需求 -

transcript.en: having to look in different places to find food, for example,
transcript.zh: 例如，必须在不同的地方寻找食物，

transcript.en: and coping with a whole new set of dangers.
transcript.zh: 并应对一系列新的危险。

transcript.en: Then over in Germany at the Max Planck Institute,
transcript.zh: 在德国马克斯·普朗克研究所，

transcript.en: there's another biologist called Catarina Miranda who's done some experiments with blackbirds living in urban and rural areas.
transcript.zh: 还有另一位名叫Catarina Miranda的生物学家，他对生活在城市和农村地区的乌鸦做了一些实验。

transcript.en: And she's been looking not at their anatomy but at their behaviour.
transcript.zh: 她不是通过解剖，而是通过乌鸦的行为来了解它们。

transcript.en: So as you might expect,
transcript.zh: 正如大家能想到的，

transcript.en: she's found that the urban blackbirds tend to be quite bold
transcript.zh: 她发现城市地区的乌鸦往往非常大胆

transcript.en: they're prepared to face up to a lot of threats that would frighten away their country counterparts.
transcript.zh: 因为它们随时准备面对这种威胁，而农村地区的乌鸦一般都会被吓跑。

transcript.en: But there's one type of situation that does seem to frighten the urban blackbirds,
transcript.zh: 但是有一种情况确实会吓到城市地区的乌鸦，

transcript.en: and that's anything new - anything they haven't experienced before.
transcript.zh: 就是新的事物 - 它们以前从没有经历过的事物。

transcript.en: And if you think about it,
transcript.zh: 大家仔细想一想，

transcript.en: that's quite sensible for a bird living in the city.
transcript.zh: 这对生活在城市里的鸟类来说是一种非常明智的行为。

transcript.en: Jonathan Atwell, in Indiana University,
transcript.zh: 印第安纳大学的Jonathan Atwell

transcript.en: is looking at how a range of animals respond to urban environments.
transcript.zh: 正在研究一系列动物对城市环境的反应。

transcript.en: He's found that when they're under stress,
transcript.zh: 他发现，当动物处于压力之下时，

transcript.en: their endocrine systems react by reducing the amount of hormones such as corticosterone into their blood.
transcript.zh: 它们的内分泌系统通过减少血液中皮质酮等激素的含量来做出反应。

transcript.en: It's a sensible- seeming adaptation.
transcript.zh: 这似乎是一种明智的适应。

transcript.en: A rat that gets scared every time a subway train rolls past won't be very successful.
transcript.zh: 每次地铁驶过都感到害怕的老鼠就没有这种适应性。

transcript.en: There's just one more study I'd like to mention which is by Sarah Partan and her team,
transcript.zh: 我还想再提一下Sarah Partan和她的团队进行的研究，

transcript.en: and they’ve been looking at how squirrels communicate in an urban environment,
transcript.zh: 关于松鼠在城市环境中的沟通方式，

transcript.en: and they've found that a routine part of their communication is carried out by waving their tails.
transcript.zh: 他们发现，松鼠的例行沟通方式是摆动它们的尾巴。

transcript.en: You do also see this in the country,
transcript.zh: 在乡村也可以看到这种现象，

transcript.en: but it's much more prevalent in cities,
transcript.zh: 但是在城市里更普遍，

transcript.en: possibly because it's effective in a noisy environment.
transcript.zh: 可能是因为这种沟通方式在嘈杂的环境中更有效。

transcript.en: So what are the long-term implications of this?
transcript.zh: 那么，这会带来什么长期影响呢？

transcript.en: One possibility is that we may see completely new species developing in cities.
transcript.zh: 一种可能是，城市中可能会出现全新的物种。

transcript.en: But on the other hand,
transcript.zh: 但另一方面，

transcript.en: it's possible that not all of these adaptations will be permanent.
transcript.zh: 并不是所有的适应都是永久性的。

transcript.en: Once the animal's got accustomed to its new environment,
transcript.zh: 一旦动物习惯了它的新环境，

transcript.en: it may no longer need the features it's developed.
transcript.zh: 它就不再需要所养成的习惯。

transcript.en: So, now we've had a look …
transcript.zh: 现在，让我们来了解一下……
